experiment: P1c hierarchical risk-benefit router with per-class Neyman-Pearson budget
hypothesis: Separating false-positive risk from expert benefit and selecting per-class coverage directly under an FPR-increment budget recovers useful expert coverage without losing P1b specificity.
frozen: role hashes and calibration identity split

models.risk_target: target-negative, expert probability exceeds main probability, and expert probability crosses the frozen target threshold
models.benefit_target: expert binary log loss plus 0.05 is lower than main binary log loss

selection.score_cutoff: safety quantile corresponding to the candidate coverage
selection.objective: maximize mean target recall gain at 10 and 50 dB
selection.fallback: per-target alpha=0 and coverage=0 if no candidate is safe

track_b_recalibrated.threshold_source: calibration safety identities only, separately for base and selected final probabilities

overall_gate: both tracks must pass before P2

roles.fit: first identity-disjoint calibration half, all nine paired power views
roles.safety: second identity-disjoint calibration half, all nine paired power views
roles.evaluation: tune identities, all nine paired power views
